title: Publisher Traps — Microsoft, Oracle, IBM, SAP, Adobe

narrations.text: Publisher-Specific Traps. Where SAM Projects Fail Audits — Exam Favorites
Publisher rules are where SAM projects fail audits. Exam questions are conceptual: "Which metric applies?" "Why is Oracle count higher than installs?" Not menu-path trivia.

Microsoft Traps. SQL Server: Per-CORE licensing — physical cores × core factor, MIN 4 cores/socket Virtualization: License the HOST, not the VM (unless SA + mobility) M365 Suite Overlap: E3 + E5 + F3 + Apps = double-counting risk Downgrade Rights: EXIST but must be documented on entitlement Core Factor Table: Must be current for SQL Server reconciliation True-Up: Annual true-up window — missing it = full retail pricing.

Oracle Traps (Highest Audit Risk). Core Factor Table: Per processor family — outdated table = wrong count Server-Level Licensing: License the PHYSICAL SERVER, not the VM Hard Partitioning: Only certified tech (OVM, LPAR) limits scope 10% Rule: NOT a rule — soft partitioning = full server licensing Named User Plus: Minimums per processor (usually 25 NUP/processor) LMS Scripts: Oracle's audit instrument — your reconciliation must match Java: Now subscription-based — separate from DB licensing.

IBM Traps. PVU (Processor Value Unit): Table per CPU model — must match exactly Sub-Capacity Licensing: Requires ILMT (IBM License Metric Tool) evidence ILMT: Must be deployed, configured, reporting — no ILMT = full capacity RVU (Resource Value Unit): For some middleware — different metric Bundles: Multiple products in one license — component tracking critical.

SAP Traps. Named User Types: Developer, Professional, Limited Professional, ESS — each priced differently Indirect / Digital Access: LIVE audit battleground — non-SAP apps accessing SAP data Engine Metrics: By revenue, employees, orders — not user count Classification: User type must match actual usage — misclassification = audit finding LAW (License Administration Workbench): SAP's audit tool.

Adobe Traps. VIP / ETLA: Named-user subscription model Shared Device License: Different from named user — labs, classrooms Creative Cloud Suite Roll-Up: Components roll up to CC suite Document Cloud: Per-document pricing (not per user) True-Up: Annual — unused licenses don't roll over.

ServiceNow (Self-Licensing). Subscription by product line + fulfilled user / approved requester Over-consumption = BILLED, not audited — treat as cost-control Plugin entitlements: com.snc.sams, com.snc.itsm, com.snc.hrsd, etc. Instance-level vs user-level metrics — know which applies.

EXAM GUIDANCE: Expect conceptual questions: • "Which metric applies to SQL Server?" → Per-core • "Why is Oracle count higher than install count?" → Core factor + server licensing • "What evidence does IBM sub-capacity require?" → ILMT • "What is SAP indirect access?" → Non-SAP apps reading SAP data NOT: "Which menu path creates an entitlement?"
